findings.claim: Removing the `q > 0` filter makes entries the client explicitly rejected (`q=0`) eligible to match, violating RFC 9110 §12.5.1 and diverging from the compress middleware.
findings.rationale: Per RFC 9110 §12.5.1 a quality value of 0 means "not acceptable". With the filter gone, a header like `Accept-Encoding: gzip;q=0` (or `*;q=0`) will still sort into `sortedAccepts` and `supports.find(...)` can return `gzip`, so `defaultMatch` hands back a representation the client said it would not accept instead of falling through to `defaultSupport`. The sort itself is unaffected (q=0 entries sort last), so the bug only surfaces when a rejected type is the only/best supported match — which is exactly the case the removed comment and the compress middleware guard against. I'm fairly confident this is a behavioral regression unless the filtering was intentionally moved to every caller.
